response.reason: The three generic structures test TEAM_B's (away team's) FOR-side attacking metrics against a similar-opponent cohort in isolation — one metric each, no conditions, no specified profile axis. The candidate is structurally distinct on two dimensions: (1) it belongs to OPPONENT_PROFILE_INTERACTION, meaning the cohort is explicitly defined by TEAM_A's defensive/discipline profile axes (goals conceded, shots on target conceded, shots inside box conceded, fouls committed, yellow cards), not generic opponent similarity; and (2) it tests a joint multi-metric bundle (shots_on_target + big_chances + shots_inside_box) as a coherent attacking-quality cluster rather than three independent single-metric questions. The mechanism requires both TEAM_B's attacking output AND TEAM_A's defensive openness to be measured together — a two-characteristic interaction the generics do not capture. The shared surface (SIMILAR_OPPONENT_COHORT, FOR, ALL_PRIOR, overlapping metrics) is real but the incremental structure is not cosmetic: the profile-axis grounding changes what the cohort actually selects.
